title: Fennel, walnut and white bean patties

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Beans, walnuts, feta, egg, breadcrumbs, yoghurt and fresh produce are all ordinary kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient, including the walnuts and feta, is an everyday item at any mainstream UK supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, grater, bowl and masher, and grating, mashing and shallow-frying patties suit a confident beginner.

works.reason: Softened fennel, two tins of mashed beans, egg and breadcrumbs make a firm enough mix for eight patties, a sensible amount for four with the tomatoes and yoghurt.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers grating, chopping, the 5-minute fennel fry and shaping, and 15 minutes matches frying the patties, which suits a quick dinner.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the oil split as 1 plus 2 plus 1 tbsp and the lemon zest and juice, is used, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Grated fennel, backed up by fennel seeds, flavours the patties, and a warm pan-fried supper with the last tomatoes suits late September.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English with practical tips like cooking in batches.

hearty_healthy.reason: Beans, walnuts, feta and egg give protein, served with tomatoes and yoghurt as a satisfying family meal.
